objective: Add first-class contracts for external catalog context, discovery candidates and human review feedback, explainability evidence, and explicit analysis modalities.

baseline.description: Architecture documented these capabilities but lacked executable domain contracts.

expected_improvement: Prevent human feedback from silently becoming training truth.
Make explainability and modality consumption explicit registry-facing concepts.

evidence: Executable dataclasses validate catalog provenance/evaluation role, candidate/review versioning, controlled feedback dataset identity, explainability alignment, and modality uniqueness.

findings: Architecture-only statements are insufficient to prevent semantic drift; executable contracts provide fail-fast boundaries.
Catalog context is evidence, not implicit ground truth.
Training/validation feedback requires explicit dataset version.
Missing modalities must be represented by contract state rather than fabricated.

knowledge_carried_forward: No GPU/LLM/distributed implementation is introduced by these contracts.
